Implementation Plan

Implementation plan: stuck-states P5b, one consolidated follow-up issue per PR security pass cycle (`SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED`)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `5144a729c567f31bc11a16b66b42da67582c1f87`, symbolic branch `orchestrator/project-8291` (integration branch metadata `orchestrator/project-8291`, mismatch `false`). This is an orchestrator-managed child of #8291 (local ID `p5-consolidated-followup`). P5a (delta re-audit and carry-forward) is already on this ref, so this plan delivers item 4 of the "P5 — Per-PR security pass convergence" section in `docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends security_audit.sh issues-mode follow-up filer
Scope-mode justification: The stuck-states plan (G5, Q13: A, P5 item 4) fixes the scope: one follow-up issue per cycle listing all of that cycle's new findings, with the same `Integration branch:` and `Depends on` metadata as today, and severity gating unchanged. The work extends the existing filer in `scripts/security_audit.sh`: its Python planner, the follow-up index TSV and the `gh issue create` loop. It also extends the existing follow-up readers so they recognise more than one marker. No new script, workflow, supervisor or API call is added. Under the Boil the Lake rule, also updating both readers (the review gate's open-follow-up check and the audit's dedupe) is the complete option, and it is only a few lines each. Without it, findings two to n of a consolidated issue would look "missing", the merge would be held with `followups_missing`, and the next audit would refile them. That is a correctness problem (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), so it is in scope.

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- **Script change:** extends existing scripts only (`scripts/security_audit.sh`, `scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh`). No new script.
- **Entry point:** `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml`, step "Run security audit". It runs on `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` with `pr_number`, which the review gate in `review_autofix.yml` dispatches. The only wiring change is two env rows on that step.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none needed (§20.C).
- **DB work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry:** none, because no new single-use or long-running script is added.

## Functions or modules to implement

1. **`scripts/security_audit.sh`: switch parsing**, next to the existing `SECURITY_AUDIT_PASS_FINDINGS_OUT` / `SECURITY_AUDIT_TARGET_REF` blocks (about lines 405-412 and 535):
   - `SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED="${SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED:-true}"`. Truthy values are `1/true/yes/on`, case-insensitive; anything else is off.
   - `SECURITY_AUDIT_PASS_PR_NUMBER="${SECURITY_AUDIT_PASS_PR_NUMBER:-}"`. Keep it only if it matches `^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$`; otherwise blank it and print a `::warning::`.
   - Derived `SECURITY_AUDIT_CONSOLIDATE_ACTIVE=true` only when all of these hold: output mode is `issues`, `SECURITY_AUDIT_TARGET_REF` is non-empty, the PR number is valid, and the switch is truthy. Otherwise it is `false`, which is today's per-finding path.
   - Both new variables carry defaults in the helper (§8). A run under an older `security-audit.yml` that does not export the PR number therefore keeps today's behaviour exactly.
   - Log one line: `security-audit: followup_mode=<consolidated|per_finding> pr=<n|none>`.

2. **`scripts/security_audit.sh`: Python planner** (the heredoc starting at about line 3332). Pass the active flag, the PR number and `HEAD_SHA` as new trailing `sys.argv` entries, read with the existing `len(sys.argv) > N` guard style.
   - **Dedupe reader (always on, both modes).** Keep today's `marker_regex.search(body)` match. Also collect every exact marker line in the body's *leading block*: the run of consecutive lines from line 1 that fully match `^<!-- ai:security-finding:(\S+) -->$`. Every ID in that block counts as existing, and `existing_finding_numbers[id]` is the issue number. A legacy body has exactly one leading marker, so its result is unchanged.
   - **Consolidated planning** (active only). When `planned_followups` is non-empty, write one body file, `followup-consolidated.md`:
     - The leading block: one `<!-- ai:security-finding:<id> -->` line per planned finding, in finding order.
     - `Refs #<tracker>`, a blank line, then `Generated by \`.github/workflows/security-audit.yml\`.`
     - `- Pull request: #<pr>`, `- Audited head: \`<head_sha>\``, `- Integration branch: \`<target_ref>\``. The last is the same line `resolve_integration_ref.sh` reads today.
     - A `## Findings` section. For each finding: a `### <n>. <finding_id>` heading, then Category, Severity, Confidence and Location bullets, then the exploit scenario and recommendation.
     - Title: `truncate_title(f"[security-audit] PR #{pr}: {k} findings at {head_sha[:12]}")`.
   - **Consolidated index row.** Existing-finding rows stay byte-identical (`-\t-\t<file_key>\t<number>`), so today's fail-closed check "existing follow-up has no verified issue number" still applies. Then write one row: `<body_path>\t<title>\tmulti:<k1>+<k2>...\t0`. It lists the distinct `file_key`s of the planned findings in first-seen order; hex keys never contain `+`.
   - `FOLLOWUP_CREATE_COUNT`: 1 when the consolidated row exists, otherwise 0.
   - The tracker comment gains one line, only when active: `- Follow-up mode: consolidated (<k> findings in one issue)`.
   - When the mode is not active, every output (bodies, index, env, comment) is byte-identical to today.

3. **`scripts/security_audit.sh`: create loop** (about lines 3607-3642). For a row whose file-key column starts with `multi:`:
   - Split it on `+`. Pick the dependency as the highest numeric value of `LAST_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE[key]` over those keys, and append at most one `- Depends on: #<n>` line. `scripts/security_dependency.py` holds an issue with more than one such line (`invalid or repeated security dependency`), so it must be one.
   - Create the issue with the same `gh issue create --label ai:security`, the same URL and number verification, and no retry wrapper (the existing non-idempotent comment applies).
   - Then set `LAST_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE[key]=<new number>` for every key.
   - Single-key rows are unchanged.

4. **`scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh` `single_pass_open_followup_ids()`** (about lines 328-359). Replace `.body | split("\n")[0]` with the leading-block marker lines: split the body on `\n`, keep lines from the start while each matches `^<!-- ai:security-finding:[^ >]+ -->$` (with trailing whitespace trimmed), then flatten across issues before the existing `any($issue_markers[]; ...)`.
   - The author, open-state, `pull_request == null` and `Integration branch:` filters are unchanged.
   - A legacy body still yields only its first line, so existing results are unchanged.
   - This one change covers both callers: gate-mode current-head findings (`single_pass_open_followups`) and report-mode carry-forward.
   - Update the function's header comment.
   - Severity gating and every `hold_reason` stay unchanged. A findings result still means hold=true until the head changes, and high, critical and unrated findings still block.

5. **`.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` step "Run security audit"**, add env rows:
   - `SECURITY_AUDIT_PASS_PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr_number || '' }}`
   - `SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED: ${{ vars.SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED || 'true' }}`
   - Add a 2-space-indented comment citing stuck-states P5b. The file is 32,645 bytes, far below the 480,000-byte guard.

6. **README**: add a `SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED` row after the `SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_DELTA_ENABLED` row in both tables (around lines 242 and 2820): default `true`, used by `security-audit`, with `false` restoring one issue per finding.

7. **`agents.d/stuck-states-p5b-consolidated-followup.md`**: one block, `<!-- agents: section="Workflow architecture" -->`, describing the switch, the leading marker block, the single `Depends on`, and the reader changes. No new log prefix, because the existing `security-audit:` line is extended.

8. **`changelog.d/stuck-states-p5b-consolidated-followup.md`**: `<!-- changelog: changed -->` plus one bullet with `Refs #8291`, never a closing keyword (§21).

## Data structures affected
- **Follow-up issue body (consolidated variant):** N leading `<!-- ai:security-finding:<id> -->` lines, `Refs #<tracker>`, `- Pull request: #<pr>`, `- Audited head:`, `- Integration branch:`, at most one `- Depends on: #<n>`, then `## Findings`.
- **`followup-index.tsv`:** a new `multi:`-prefixed file-key value on the consolidated row only.
- **Summary line:** `security-audit: tracker=#… findings=… followups_created=… finding_ids_b64=…` keeps its format, so the report-step `sed` parsers in `security-audit.yml` lines 534-535 still match. `followups_created` counts issues (0 or 1) in consolidated mode.
- **Unchanged:** the `ai:single-issue-security-pass:v1` marker and the `Finding IDs (base64 JSON):` / `Audited findings` payloads.

## API or interface changes
- New repo variable `SINGLE_ISSUE_SECURITY_PASS_CONSOLIDATE_ENABLED`, default `true`.
- New helper env `SECURITY_AUDIT_PASS_PR_NUMBER`, default empty.
- No new workflow inputs, so consumer wrappers need no changes.
